memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When the people heard these distressing words, they began to mourn and no one put on any ornaments. For the Lord had said to Moses, 'Tell the Israelites, "You are a stiff-necked people. If I were to go with you even for a moment, I might destroy you. Now take off your ornaments and I will decide what to do with you."' So the Israelites stripped off their ornaments at Mount Horeb." - Exod 33:4-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Something has shifted. The people who were dancing around a calf are now mourning. The ornaments that were melted down into an idol are now stripped off in grief.

This is what real repentance looks like from the outside. It is not merely feeling bad about consequences. It is grief over the loss of God Himself. What broke them was not the threat of hardship but the words "I will not go with you."

Ask yourself honestly what troubles you most about your sin. That it might be found out? That it costs you something? Or that it grieves God and dulls your fellowship with Him? Paul distinguishes godly sorrow, which leads to repentance and life, from worldly sorrow, which just leads to death (2 Cor 7:10).

Notice too the uncertainty: "I will decide what to do with you." God does not immediately reassure them. There is a waiting, and the waiting is part of the work God is doing in them.

If you are in a season where God feels silent after failure, do not rush to manufacture comfort. Let the sorrow do its work. God is not withdrawing from you — He is drawing something out of you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What grieves you most about your own sin?
2. Have you ever mourned the loss of closeness with God?
3. What "ornaments" might God be asking you to lay down?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me sorrow that leads to life. More than comfort, I want closeness with You again. Amen.
